decisions.reason: The accepted proposal explicitly preserves Danish style names while changing the document default to English, and the candidate's same-message INTRODUCE already captures the Danish style-name requirement completely.
Changing the document default language does not alter the requirement for stable rendering across users or its supported Word environment.
The source decision concerns default and style-name languages, not layout or style stability when transferring legacy content.
The language decision neither resolves the existing table-adjustment conflict nor changes pasted-table or column-containment behavior.
Default document language has no logically entailed effect on the required manual line-break behavior after pasted content.
The source decision does not change bullet sizing, visual balance, or vertical alignment.
The accepted language configuration does not change Tab-based list hierarchy, indentation, or alignment behavior.
Using Danish style names does not necessarily remove or change the required PBU prefix or its applicability.
The language decision does not alter the prescribed style catalog or the rule to deploy the style system consistently across templates.
